name: cavemio-tag-input
title: Tag input
description: The invite field, done properly: typed letters grow a chip round themselves, pasted lists spill out of the caret, and a duplicate flies into its twin.

cavemio.accessibility:
- The input is a combobox with a listbox of suggestions: arrows move the highlight, Enter picks it (the first match is ready while you type), Escape closes the list and Down opens it again.
- Chips are a list. Left arrow or Backspace at the start of the input moves to the last chip; arrows, Home and End move between chips; Backspace or Enter edits one, Delete removes it, Escape returns to the input. Each remove button is named after its chip.
- Adds, duplicates, invalid values, removals and resolved names are announced in a status region outside the field. The error under the field is linked to the input with aria-describedby.
- Every change notes where the chips sit at the keystroke, lets React lay out the new order, then glides each chip from its old place with an additive transform, so a name that resolves while a paste is still landing adds its own glide instead of restarting anything. Leaving and flying copies live in an overlay so the list never waits for them. Nothing runs between changes.
- On touch screens the input uses 16px text so phones don't zoom into it; the chip's letters scale down to 13px as the shell grows.
- Reduced motion adds, removes and resolves in place; colour, icons and the line under the field still say what happened.
cavemio.previewNote: Interactive local fixture. Data and async results are simulated in the preview; the caller supplies application services.

props.name: value
props.description: – · Controlled tags: { id, value, label?, image?, error? }.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: – · Every add, remove, edit and resolve. Tags with an error are included so you can show them; filter them out before sending.

props.name: validate
props.description: – · Return a message to mark a value invalid. The chip turns red and the message shows under the field.

props.name: resolve
props.description: – · Looks a value up once it's added. Return a label (and image) for the chip to morph into, or null to leave it.

props.name: suggestions
props.description: – · A list to filter by value, label and description, or a function (which may be async) that finds matches. Values already added are left out.

props.name: normalize
props.description: – · Applied before checking and comparing, e.g. lower-casing addresses so duplicates are caught.

props.name: separators
props.description: /[,;\n]+/ · What splits typed and pasted text. Add \s for addresses.

props.name: max
props.description: – · How many tags the field takes. More shakes the field and shows limitMessage.

props.name: limitMessage
props.description: "No room for more" · The line shown when a value doesn't fit under max.

props.name: createLabel
props.description: (t) => Add “${t}” · The suggestion row that adds what's typed as it is. null hides it.

props.name: collapse
props.description: – · Lines to show while the field is out of focus; the rest fold into a "+N" count.

props.name: label
props.description: "Add tags" · Accessible name of the field and its list.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: – · Shown while the field is empty.

props.name: hint
props.description: – · A line under the field. Errors and notices take its place while they last.

props.name: name
props.description: – · Submits the valid values, comma-separated, with a form.

props.name: disabled
props.description: false · Nothing can be added, edited or removed.

props.name: ref
props.description: – · paste(text), focus() and clear(), e.g. for a "Paste from spreadsheet" button or clearing after sending.

features.title: Typed text becomes a chip in place
features.description: The letters stay exactly where they were while a thin line shell grows around them.

features.title: Paste a list
features.description: Pasted text is split on commas, semicolons and new lines (or your own pattern), and chips spill out of the caret one by one.

features.title: Duplicates and invalid values
features.description: A repeat flies into the chip it repeats. An invalid value lands red, shakes and says why.

features.title: Addresses become names
features.description: With resolve(), “maya@fernhill.co” morphs into “Maya Chen” as her initials open in.

features.title: Suggestions and limits
features.description: Search suggestions as you type, an “Add …” row for new values, and a max that keeps the field to the seats left.

features.title: Edit and collapse
features.description: Backspace selects the last chip and a second press makes it editable. Out of focus, lines past a number fold into a rolling “+4”.

states.title: type
states.description: Enter, Tab, a separator or leaving the field turns the text into a chip in place: its letters scale from the input's size to the chip's without moving, and the shell grows from their outline to the full pill in 480ms while the remove button scales in.

states.title: paste
states.description: A pasted list (or one passed to the handle's paste) is split and each chip flies out of the caret 50ms after the last, from 0.86 scale and a 4px blur, 560ms each.

states.title: duplicate
states.description: A value that's already there flies as a copy into its twin and dissolves as it arrives (a pasted one first turns up, in its turn, where it would have landed); the twin bumps to 1.08 with a slight overshoot and its ring flashes. The line under the field says "… is already here" for 2.6s.

states.title: invalid
states.description: When validate() returns a message the chip lands with a red ring, an alert icon and a 380ms shake; the message stays under the field until the chip is fixed or removed.

states.title: resolve
states.description: While resolve() runs the chip's icon slot shows a spinner; then the label morphs from the address to the name, the initials open in and the chip's shell eases to its new width while the chips after it glide.

states.title: pick
states.description: Suggestions unfold from the field's edge; the highlight glides between rows. Choosing one carries its name from the row into its new chip in 480ms, where the chip's own letters take over.

states.title: edit
states.description: Backspace or Enter on a chip, or a second click or tap on a selected one, shrinks its shell back round the letters and fades it; the address glides from where the chip was into the input with the caret at its end.

states.title: collapse
states.description: With collapse set, leaving the field folds every line past that number: hidden chips fade through a blur, the field's height eases and a "+N" pill rolls in after the last chip that shows. Focus brings them back.
